people.summary: Maria Donata's father, who lived in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and had died by January 1884. He is known from a single line in his daughter's marriage act.
people.story:
Giuseppe Circelli is known from one line. When his daughter Maria Donata married in January 1884, the clerk recorded her as the daughter "del fu Giuseppe", the late Giuseppe, who had lived in the town during his lifetime.[^marriage-1884] By then he was dead, and so was his wife.

Because neither parent was alive, the act records that consent to the marriage came from the bride's family council, the consiglio di famiglia, a group of relatives who stood in for parents who had died.[^marriage-1884]

That is all the records in this collection say about him. His age, his trade and his date of death are not known. Circelli was a common surname in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, and the town's civil registers survive on the Antenati portal, so his death record, and perhaps his marriage, should be findable there.[^research-md]

media.transcription:
ATTI DI MATRIMONIO. Numero 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

L'anno milleottocento ottantaquattro addì ventisette di gennaio a ore anti meridiane nove e minuti cinquantacinque, nella Casa comunale di Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, aperta al pubblico.

Avanti di me Mosa [o Morra?] Giuseppe, Sindaco, Uffiziale dello Stato Civile, vestito in forma ufficiale sono personalmente comparsi:

1. Belfiore Lionardantonio, di anni ventitre, contadino, nato in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlio di padre ignoto, residente in [vuoto], e di madre ignota, residente in [vuoto];

2. Circelli Maria Donata, di anni ventuno, contadina, nata in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlia del fu Giuseppe, residente in vita qui, e della fu Mansolina [lettura incerta] Mita, residente in vita in detto Comune,

i quali mi hanno richiesto di unirli in matrimonio: a questo effetto mi hanno presentato il documento sotto descritto; e dall'esame di questo, nonchè di quelli già prodotti all'atto della richiesta delle pubblicazioni, i quali tutti, muniti del mio visto, inserisco nel volume degli allegati a questo registro, risultandomi nulla ostare alla celebrazione del loro matrimonio, ho letto agli sposi gli articoli centotrenta, centotrentuno e centotrentadue del Codice Civile, e quindi ho domandato allo sposo se intende di prendere in moglie la qui presente Circelli Maria Donata, e a questa se intende di prendere in marito il qui presente Belfiore Lionardantonio, ed avendomi ciascuno risposto affermativamente a piena intelligenza anche dei testimoni sotto indicati, ho pronunziato in nome della legge che i medesimi sono uniti in matrimonio.

A quest'atto sono stati presenti Reino [lettura incerta] Domenico, di anni quarantasei, guardia municipale, e Paradiso Giuseppe, di anni sessantasette, donzello municipale, entrambi residenti in questo Comune.

Il documento presentato è il certificato delle pubblicazioni da me eseguite, la prima il tredici e la seconda il venti del corrente mese di gennaio. Al matrimonio suddetto è stato prestato il consenso dal consiglio di famiglia della sposa, come risulta dall'atto di richiesta delle pubblicazioni.

Letto il presente atto agl'intervenuti, si sono meco sottoscritti i soli testimoni, essendo gli altri analfabeti.

[Firme:] Reino Domenico, testimone. Giuseppe Paradiso, testimonio. Giuseppe Mora [?]

MARRIAGE RECORDS. Number 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

In the year eighteen hundred eighty-four, on the twenty-seventh of January, at nine fifty-five in the morning, in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo, open to the public.

Before me, Giuseppe Mosa [or Morra?], Mayor and Civil Registrar, dressed in official form, there personally appeared:

1. Lionardantonio Belfiore, aged twenty-three, farm worker (contadino), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, son of an unknown father and an unknown mother (padre ignoto, madre ignota);

2. Maria Donata Circelli, aged twenty-one, farm worker (contadina), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, daughter of the late Giuseppe, who lived here in his lifetime, and of the late Mansolina [uncertain reading] Mita, who lived in this town in her lifetime,

who asked me to unite them in marriage. For this purpose they presented the document described below. Having examined it, and those already produced when the banns were requested, all of which I have stamped and placed in the volume of attachments to this register, and finding no impediment to the marriage, I read to the couple articles 130, 131 and 132 of the Civil Code. I then asked the groom whether he wished to take as his wife Maria Donata Circelli, here present, and asked her whether she wished to take as her husband Lionardantonio Belfiore, here present. Each answered yes, in the full hearing of the witnesses named below, and I pronounced them united in marriage in the name of the law.

Present at this act were Domenico Reino [uncertain reading], aged forty-six, municipal guard, and Giuseppe Paradiso, aged sixty-seven, municipal usher, both living in this town.

The document presented is the certificate of the banns I published, the first on the thirteenth and the second on the twentieth of this month of January. Consent to the marriage was given by the bride's family council, as shown in the act requesting the banns.

This act was read to those present. Only the witnesses signed it with me, the others being illiterate.

[Signatures:] Domenico Reino, witness. Giuseppe Paradiso, witness. Giuseppe Mora [?]

people.story:
Maria Donata's marriage act of January 1884 names her mother with the word fu, "the late", and records that she too had lived in San Bartolomeo in Galdo.[^marriage-1884]

Her name needs care. Earlier research on this site gave it as Marianna Mita.[^research-md] A close reading of the scan for this profile does not clearly support Marianna: the handwriting looks more like Mansolina or Marsolina, followed by a short surname that reads as Mita. Old Italian civil hands are hard to read, and a second record would settle it. Until then the tree keeps "Marianna Mita" and marks the name as uncertain.[^marriage-1884]

Nothing else is known about her yet: not her age, her parents, or when she died.

people.summary: A foundling who married Maria Donata Circelli in San Bartolomeo in Galdo in 1884. The working identification is that he is Anthony Belfiore, father of nine children in New Rochelle, who died there in 1938.
people.story:
At five minutes to ten on the morning of January 27, 1884, a twenty-three-year-old farm worker stood in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo to be married. The clerk wrote his name as Belfiore Lionardantonio. In the spaces for his parents he wrote two phrases: padre ignoto, madre ignota. Father unknown, mother unknown.[^marriage-1884]

Those phrases explain the family name. A child of unknown parents had no surname to inherit, so one was given to him. In Italy such children were often left at the ruota degli esposti, the turning wheel set into the wall of a church or hospital, and the institution or the registrar chose their names.[^ctx-ruota] Some foundling surnames marked the child as abandoned, such as Esposito. Others were simply pleasant words, and Belfiore, "beautiful flower", reads like one of these. That is very probably how Leonardantonio came by it, although his own birth and admission records have not been found. It also means the family has no link to the noble Belfiore families of other parts of Italy. The name begins with him.[^research-md]

## The wedding

The marriage act says he was born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and lived there. His bride was Maria Donata Circelli, twenty-one, also a farm worker, whose parents were both dead. Her consent came from a council of her relatives. The banns had been read on the 13th and the 20th of January. Two town employees stood as witnesses: a municipal guard aged forty-six and the town hall usher, aged sixty-seven. When the act was read back, only the witnesses signed, "the others being illiterate".[^marriage-1884]

## From Leonardantonio to Anthony

No record in this collection uses the name Leonardantonio after 1884. In America the children's father is Anthony or Antonio. The working identification on this site is that he is the same man. It is a strong case but not a proven one, and it rests on several records that point the same way.

- **The name.** Leonardantonio joins Leonardo and Antonio. Using only Antonio, and then Anthony, is an ordinary change for an Italian immigrant.
- **The children's records.** Michael's 1952 death certificate names his parents as Anthony Belfiore and Maria Circelli.[^death-michael-1952] Sammy's obituary calls the nine children's parents "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore".[^standard-star-obit] Indexed records give Frank's and Lena's parents as Antonio Belfiore and Maria D. Circelli.[^frank-index][^lena-index]
- **Citizenship.** In 1918 Michael answered the citizenship question in the column for men who became citizens through their father's naturalization while still minors, writing "Father Papers".[^ww1-michael] His father, then, was in the United States and naturalized before Michael turned twenty-one, around 1906.
- **A return voyage.** Earlier research found a 1909 Ellis Island manifest listing a "Belfiore, Antonio" from San Bartolomeo as a US citizen returning from Italy.[^manifest-1909]
- **A death.** The New York State death index lists an Anthony Belfiore who died in New Rochelle on July 11, 1938, certificate 42184.[^ny-death-index-1938]

Earlier versions of this site argued that Leonardantonio died in Italy before 1896, because Maria Donata crossed that year under her own surname. The records point the other way. Italian women kept their birth surnames in civil and travel records, so a list naming her as Circelli says nothing about her husband. And Frank, born in New Rochelle in November 1897, and Sammy, born there on Christmas Day 1899, both had a father named Anthony or Antonio.[^frank-index][^standard-star-obit]

## What we do not know

When he left San Bartolomeo, and on which ship, is unknown. The transcription of Michael's death certificate gives Michael 58 years of residence in New Rochelle, which would put Michael's arrival around 1894, two years before Maria Donata's crossing.[^death-michael-1952] Whether father and son came first is a fair question, and the 1900 census should answer it, because it asked every immigrant the year they arrived.

His burial place is also unknown. Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, where Michael was buried, is the first place to ask.

people.summary: Born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo around 1862, married Leonardantonio Belfiore in 1884, and crossed to New York on the SS Oregon in December 1896. She raised nine children in New Rochelle.
people.story:
Maria Donata Circelli could not write her name. When she married in January 1884 she was twenty-one, a farm worker, and an orphan: the clerk wrote both her parents' names after the word fu, "the late". With her parents dead, the consent for her marriage came from a council of her relatives.[^marriage-1884]

She was born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, a hill town in the province of Benevento, where Circelli is one of the old family names.[^marriage-1884][^research-md] Her husband was Leonardantonio Belfiore, a foundling two years older. Their son Michele, later Michael, was born in Italy in December 1885, or 1883 by one record.[^ww1-michael][^ww2-michael]

## The crossing

On December 2, 1896, the steamship Oregon reached New York from Genoa and Naples. On its passenger list, at line 413, was "Circelli, Maria Doreta". Earlier research recorded her age as 34, which agrees with the marriage act.[^oregon-1896-index] Doreta is very probably a clerk's version of Donata, and the source of the "Maria D." in later records.

She traveled under her own surname. That was normal for an Italian married woman, whose legal surname did not change at marriage, and it should not be read as a sign that she was a widow. Her arrival came in the last months of the first Ellis Island station, a wooden complex that burned in June 1897. Most passenger manifests from those years were lost in the fire. Lists like hers survive because the Customs Service kept its own copies.[^ctx-ellis-nps][^ctx-ellis-foundation]

Whether Michael crossed with her is not known. The full list page would show any child on the lines after hers. The page shared on this site as the Oregon list does not include her line.[^customs-list-page]

## New Rochelle

By November 1897 the family was in New Rochelle, New York, where Frank was born. Sammy followed on Christmas Day 1899.[^frank-index][^standard-star-obit] In all she raised nine children who survived to be named in Sammy's obituary: Michael, Frank, Joseph and Sammy, and Rose, Caroline, Mollie, Phyl and Mary.[^standard-star-obit] Three of the sons became golf professionals.[^standard-star-obit]

Her Circelli relatives used the same route. In March 1898 Salvatore and Michele Circelli arrived on the Alsatia, giving San Bartolomeo as their home, and in 1911 Salvatore gave New Rochelle as his destination.[^alsatia-1898][^santanna-1911] How they were related to her is not yet known.

## What we do not know

Her date and place of death have not been found. By 1972 Sammy's obituary could call his parents "the late Anthony and Maria".[^standard-star-obit] A New York death certificate under Maria, Mary or Marie Belfiore, or a burial record at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, would give the date, and should name her parents, which would help settle her mother's name.

media.caption: Marriage act no. 16, San Bartolomeo in Galdo, January 27, 1884
media.alt: The 1884 marriage act of Leonardantonio Belfiore and Maria Donata Circelli from the San Bartolomeo in Galdo civil register, as shown on the Antenati portal
media.transcription:
ATTI DI MATRIMONIO. Numero 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

L'anno milleottocento ottantaquattro addì ventisette di gennaio a ore anti meridiane nove e minuti cinquantacinque, nella Casa comunale di Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, aperta al pubblico.

Avanti di me Mosa [o Morra?] Giuseppe, Sindaco, Uffiziale dello Stato Civile, vestito in forma ufficiale sono personalmente comparsi:

1. Belfiore Lionardantonio, di anni ventitre, contadino, nato in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlio di padre ignoto, residente in [vuoto], e di madre ignota, residente in [vuoto];

2. Circelli Maria Donata, di anni ventuno, contadina, nata in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlia del fu Giuseppe, residente in vita qui, e della fu Mansolina [lettura incerta] Mita, residente in vita in detto Comune,

i quali mi hanno richiesto di unirli in matrimonio: a questo effetto mi hanno presentato il documento sotto descritto; e dall'esame di questo, nonchè di quelli già prodotti all'atto della richiesta delle pubblicazioni, i quali tutti, muniti del mio visto, inserisco nel volume degli allegati a questo registro, risultandomi nulla ostare alla celebrazione del loro matrimonio, ho letto agli sposi gli articoli centotrenta, centotrentuno e centotrentadue del Codice Civile, e quindi ho domandato allo sposo se intende di prendere in moglie la qui presente Circelli Maria Donata, e a questa se intende di prendere in marito il qui presente Belfiore Lionardantonio, ed avendomi ciascuno risposto affermativamente a piena intelligenza anche dei testimoni sotto indicati, ho pronunziato in nome della legge che i medesimi sono uniti in matrimonio.

A quest'atto sono stati presenti Reino [lettura incerta] Domenico, di anni quarantasei, guardia municipale, e Paradiso Giuseppe, di anni sessantasette, donzello municipale, entrambi residenti in questo Comune.

Il documento presentato è il certificato delle pubblicazioni da me eseguite, la prima il tredici e la seconda il venti del corrente mese di gennaio. Al matrimonio suddetto è stato prestato il consenso dal consiglio di famiglia della sposa, come risulta dall'atto di richiesta delle pubblicazioni.

Letto il presente atto agl'intervenuti, si sono meco sottoscritti i soli testimoni, essendo gli altri analfabeti.

[Firme:] Reino Domenico, testimone. Giuseppe Paradiso, testimonio. Giuseppe Mora [?]
media.translation:
MARRIAGE RECORDS. Number 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

In the year eighteen hundred eighty-four, on the twenty-seventh of January, at nine fifty-five in the morning, in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo, open to the public.

Before me, Giuseppe Mosa [or Morra?], Mayor and Civil Registrar, dressed in official form, there personally appeared:

1. Lionardantonio Belfiore, aged twenty-three, farm worker (contadino), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, son of an unknown father and an unknown mother (padre ignoto, madre ignota);

2. Maria Donata Circelli, aged twenty-one, farm worker (contadina), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, daughter of the late Giuseppe, who lived here in his lifetime, and of the late Mansolina [uncertain reading] Mita, who lived in this town in her lifetime,

who asked me to unite them in marriage. For this purpose they presented the document described below. Having examined it, and those already produced when the banns were requested, all of which I have stamped and placed in the volume of attachments to this register, and finding no impediment to the marriage, I read to the couple articles 130, 131 and 132 of the Civil Code. I then asked the groom whether he wished to take as his wife Maria Donata Circelli, here present, and asked her whether she wished to take as her husband Lionardantonio Belfiore, here present. Each answered yes, in the full hearing of the witnesses named below, and I pronounced them united in marriage in the name of the law.

Present at this act were Domenico Reino [uncertain reading], aged forty-six, municipal guard, and Giuseppe Paradiso, aged sixty-seven, municipal usher, both living in this town.

The document presented is the certificate of the banns I published, the first on the thirteenth and the second on the twentieth of this month of January. Consent to the marriage was given by the bride's family council, as shown in the act requesting the banns.

This act was read to those present. Only the witnesses signed it with me, the others being illiterate.

[Signatures:] Domenico Reino, witness. Giuseppe Paradiso, witness. Giuseppe Mora [?]

people.summary: A man from San Bartolomeo in Galdo who crossed with Michele Circelli in 1898 and was bound for New Rochelle in 1911. Probably a relative of Maria Donata, but the link is unproven.
people.story:
Salvatore Circelli crossed from Naples on the Alsatia, which sailed on February 26, 1898, and reached New York on March 19. He was twenty-eight and could not read or write. On the next line was Michele Circelli, twenty-five. Several men from San Bartolomeo were listed together on that page, and the clerk wrote the town as "S. Bartolomeo in Calore".[^alsatia-1898][^alsatia-1898-index]

Thirteen years later he crossed again. The Sant'Anna left Naples on November 14, 1911, carrying a married Salvatore Circelli, forty-two, whose final destination was New Rochelle, New York.[^santanna-1911] His two ages agree on a birth around 1869, and the second voyage ties a Circelli of San Bartolomeo directly to the town where Maria Donata's family lived.

## How was he related to Maria Donata?

Earlier research called him her brother or cousin. An online index of San Bartolomeo births lists a Salvatore born on January 1, 1869, and a Michele born on March 12, 1871, both sons of Leonardo Circelli and Rosa Pacifico.[^italyheritage-circelli] If those are the two men on the Alsatia, they were not Maria Donata's brothers, because her parents were Giuseppe Circelli and his wife. They could be cousins. The ages do not match perfectly for Michele, and the index has not been checked against the registers, so the relationship stays open.

people.summary: Traveled with Salvatore Circelli on the Alsatia in 1898. He is not Michael Belfiore: he was ten or more years older and carried a different surname.
people.story:
Michele Circelli was twenty-five when he reached New York on the Alsatia on March 19, 1898, on the line after Salvatore Circelli. Like Salvatore he could not read or write, and his home was given as San Bartolomeo.[^alsatia-1898][^alsatia-1898-index]

He is sometimes confused with Michael Belfiore, because Michele is the Italian form of Michael. He cannot be the same man. Michael was born in 1883 or 1885 and would have been about twelve or fourteen in 1898, and he was a Belfiore, not a Circelli.[^ww1-michael][^ww2-michael]

An online index of San Bartolomeo births lists a Michele Circelli born on March 12, 1871, son of Leonardo Circelli and Rosa Pacifico.[^italyheritage-circelli] That child would have been twenty-six or twenty-seven in March 1898, close to but not exactly the age on the manifest. If he is the same man, he was probably Maria Donata's cousin rather than her brother. Nothing more is known of him yet.

people.summary: The eldest son and the only one of the four brothers born in Italy. A house painter in New Rochelle for most of his life, married twice, and Seb's great-grandfather.
people.story:
Michael Kirtus Belfiore registered for the draft on September 12, 1918, the day the United States called up every man from 18 to 45.[^ctx-ww1-draft] The registrar described him as of medium height and medium build, with brown eyes and black hair. He was thirty-two, a painter, living at 114 Winyah Avenue in New Rochelle and working for an employer whose name reads as Witmark, at 8 Banks Street.[^ww1-michael]

Two answers on that card matter more than the rest. For citizenship he wrote "Father Papers", in the column for men who became citizens through a father's naturalization before they turned twenty-one. And as his nearest relative he named "(Child) Dorothy Belfiore" of 216 Hamilton Street, Bridgeport, Connecticut.[^ww1-michael] He signed the card himself: Michael, then a word he struck out, then Belfiore, with Kirtus written underneath.

## Born in Italy

He was born on December 15, but the year depends on the record. The 1918 card says 1885, and so does the transcription of his death certificate. His 1942 card says 1883.[^ww1-michael][^death-michael-1952][^ww2-michael] The 1940 census gives his age as 55, which fits 1884 or 1885.[^census-1940] His parents married in January 1884, so 1885 is the easier fit, but only his Italian birth record, probably under the name Michele, will settle it. It has not been found.

He was the only one of the four brothers born in Italy.[^standard-star-obit] When he crossed is unknown. His death certificate gives 58 years of residence, which would mean about 1894.[^death-michael-1952] The 1940 census recorded him as naturalized, which matches the 1918 card: he became a citizen through his father.[^census-1940][^ww1-michael]

## Two marriages

Dorothy, the child named on the 1918 card, was living in Bridgeport, apart from her father. Family knowledge holds that she was the daughter of an earlier marriage. The first wife's name is not known.[^family-knowledge]

His second wife was Frances Towey, an Irish-American born in New York in 1897.[^ssdi-frances][^family-knowledge] In April 1940 the census found them at 488 North Avenue, New Rochelle, with their sons Edward, nineteen, and Joseph, seventeen. Michael had left school after seventh grade. He was out of work and had been looking for thirty-six weeks; in 1939 he had worked sixteen weeks as a building painter and earned $200. Frances worked twenty hours a week in a high school cafeteria and had earned $420. Joseph, still in school, worked as a grocery delivery boy.[^census-1940]

## The non-golfing brother

While his three younger brothers became golf professionals at clubs from Daytona Beach to Grosse Pointe, Michael stayed in New Rochelle and painted. Sammy's obituary called him "their non-golfing brother".[^standard-star-obit]

In April 1942 he registered again, in the "old man's registration" for men born between 1877 and 1897.[^ctx-ww2-fourth] He lived at 48 Coligni Avenue and had no telephone. His employer was Alfred A. Last of 141 Chauncey Avenue. The person who would always know his address was "Wife, same address".[^ww2-michael]

He died at New Rochelle Hospital on January 16, 1952, of arteriosclerotic heart disease, and was buried at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery three days later. Frances was the informant on his death certificate. His last address was 46 Mechanic Street.[^death-michael-1952] His grandson William, Seb's uncle, was not yet two.[^family-william]

media.alt: Newspaper clipping of Sammy Belfore's 1972 obituary from The Standard-Star, with a photograph of him swinging a club
media.summary: Summary (not a transcription). Headline: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers". Reports that Sammy, 72, died in Daytona Beach after a long illness; that he had changed the spelling of his name and had long been pro at the Seabreeze Golf and Tennis Club; that he was born on Christmas Day 1899 in New Rochelle to "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore", one of four brothers and five sisters; that Sammy, Frank and Joseph took up golf professionally when most pros were foreign-born; that Sam started as assistant pro at Wykagyl Country Club and went to Seabreeze in 1948 after 36 years in golf; that Frank ran the golf shop at the Daytona club and Joe was pro at Grosse Pointe, Michigan; that Frank, Joe and "their non-golfing brother, Michael" had died. Survivors: son Sammy Jr. (Daytona Beach), daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming (Birmingham, Mich.), sisters Rose and Caroline Belfiore (Wykagyl Gardens), Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew (Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle), Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro (Hartford, Conn.), Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio (Hollywood, Fla.), and three grandchildren. Frances Towey was born on September 17, 1897, in New York.[^ssdi-frances][^census-1940] Towey is an Irish surname, and the family remembers her as Irish-American.[^family-knowledge] Her parents' names have not been found yet. Her death certificate, which has been ordered, should give them and their birthplaces.

She married Michael Belfiore, who was about twelve years older and had a daughter from an earlier marriage. The date is not known, but their son Edward was born around 1920.[^census-1940]

In April 1940 she was forty-two, had finished eighth grade, and was working twenty hours a week in a high school cafeteria. She had earned $420 the year before, more than Michael, who was out of work. The family lived at 488 North Avenue, New Rochelle, with their sons Edward and Joseph.[^census-1940]

When Michael died in January 1952, she gave the details for his death certificate as Frances M. Belfiore, of 46 Mechanic Street.[^death-michael-1952] She died in New Rochelle on April 5, 1967, aged sixty-nine.[^ssdi-frances]

people.story:
Everything known about this Dorothy comes from one line. On September 12, 1918, her father Michael named "(Child) Dorothy Belfiore", of 216 Hamilton Street, Bridgeport, Connecticut, as his nearest relative.[^ww1-michael] Family knowledge holds that she was the daughter of Michael's first marriage.[^family-knowledge]

She is easy to confuse with another Dorothy Belfiore: Dorothy Hennessey, who married Michael's son Joseph and is Seb's grandmother. They are different women, a generation apart.

## What happened to her?

She has not been found in any later record. Earlier versions of this site suggested she died in the 1918 influenza epidemic, which did reach Bridgeport within two weeks of Michael's registration.[^ctx-flu-ct] That is possible, but nothing yet supports it. Her absence from Michael's household in 1940 means little, because by then she would have been an adult and may have married. She may also have been raised by her mother's family in Bridgeport.

Her birth year is not known. Earlier versions of the tree showed about 1914, without a source, and the card here keeps that estimate with a question mark.

people.story:
In April 1940 Joseph Belfiore was seventeen, in his second year of high school, and working fourteen hours a week as a delivery boy for a grocery store. He lived with his parents, Michael and Frances, and his brother Edward at 488 North Avenue in New Rochelle.[^census-1940]

That census age places his birth between April 1922 and April 1923, in New York. Earlier versions of this site gave about 1928, without a source. The census is better evidence, and the dates shown here follow it.

## Two Josephs

The family has two men named Joseph in consecutive generations, and they are easy to mix up. Joe Belfore the golfer, head professional at the Country Club of Detroit, was Michael's brother. This Joseph was Michael's son. Earlier versions of this site said he was named after this uncle, following the Italian custom of naming sons after relatives. That is likely, but no record states it. The golfer used the spelling Belfore; this Joseph kept Belfiore.

## Family

He married Dorothy Hennessey, who is remembered as Irish-American. They had four children: Robert, Seb's father; William; Karen; and Beth.[^family-knowledge]

He died in 1986. The family places his death in Valrico, Florida. A Social Security Death Index entry for a Joseph Belfiore who died in April 1986 gives a last residence in West Babylon, New York, and a number issued in Maryland. That entry has not been confirmed as his, and the two places need reconciling.[^family-knowledge][^ssdi-joseph]

people.summary: Born in New Rochelle in 1897, one of the three golfing brothers. He ran the golf shop at the Seabreeze club in Daytona Beach alongside Sammy, and died in Daytona Beach in 1968.
people.story:
The one photograph in this collection that names Frank shows him behind the counter of a golf shop in Daytona Beach in early 1948. He stands on the right, in a pale shirt, with his brother Sammy across the room. The magazine caption reads, simply, "Sammy Belfore and (R) brother Frank in Seabreeze shop".[^golfdom-1948-02] In the article beside it Sammy wrote that his new, well-equipped golf shop would be under the supervision of his brother Frank.[^golfdom-1948-02]

Frank was born in New Rochelle in November 1897, about eleven months after his mother reached New York. An indexed record names his parents as Antonio Belfiore and Maria D. Circelli.[^frank-index] He was one of three brothers who became golf professionals, at a time when, as Sammy's obituary put it, the profession was dominated by men from abroad.[^standard-star-obit]

Little else about his career is documented here. Sammy's obituary says that "Frank took over the golf shop at the club in Daytona".[^standard-star-obit] Earlier research found that he died in Daytona Beach on April 21, 1968.[^frank-death] By the time Sammy died in 1972, Frank was described as dead.[^standard-star-obit]

A family photograph of three men in light suits on a golf course is believed to show Sammy, Frank and Joe together. Nobody in it has been identified with certainty.[^golf-brothers-photo]

people.summary: Head professional at the Country Club of Detroit for many years, author of Golfing Aids (1940), and by earlier research a two-time Michigan PGA champion. Not to be confused with his nephew Joseph, Seb's grandfather.
people.story:
In 1940 the professional at the Country Club of Detroit published a slim green booklet of lessons, priced at twenty-five cents. The title page reads Golfing Aids, by Joe Belfore, Professional, Country Club of Detroit. One surviving copy is signed "Sincerely, Joe Belfore, Detroit, Michigan, April 4, 1940", beside a photograph of the author in a white shirt and tie, his chin resting on his hand. It opens with the grip and stance, and its pages show him demonstrating the drive and a fairway wood.[^golfing-aids-1940] That copy came from the PGA REACH collection and was sold in 2025 with a letter of provenance signed by Bob Denney, the PGA of America's historian emeritus.[^pga-reach-letter-2025]

Joe was one of three Belfiore brothers from New Rochelle who became golf professionals, at a time when most professionals and club makers in America were from abroad, "usually Scotch", as Sammy's obituary put it.[^standard-star-obit] Like Sammy, he wrote the name Belfore.

## Florida winters, Michigan summers

In January 1929 he was working as a professional at Daytona Highlands in Florida, the same club as Sammy. At a tournament at Mount Plymouth that month, his pairing finished on 150, level with Sammy's.[^dbnj-1929-01-07] Like many northern club professionals, he seems to have worked in Florida for the winter season.

His main post was the Country Club of Detroit in Grosse Pointe Farms, Michigan, where he was head professional and ran the golf shop.[^golfing-aids-1940][^ccd-minutes-1963] Earlier research, drawing on the Michigan PGA's centennial history, records that he won the Michigan PGA championship in 1933 and 1937 and served as president of the Michigan PGA in 1959 and 1960. The same research found him in the field for the 1927 Metropolitan Open with Walter Hagen and Gene Sarazen, and in Golfdom magazine in January 1934.[^mipga-centennial][^nyt-1927][^golfdom-1934-01] In May 1948 the Daytona Beach papers reported that he had qualified for the PGA tournament at St. Louis.[^dbmj-1948-05-21]

## 1963

Joe died in 1963 after a long illness. On October 29 the club's Board of Governors set up a committee to find a professional "for the position of Golf Professional left vacant by the death of Joe Belfore". Mrs. Belfore had written the board a letter of appreciation. The board voted her $750 "as a gift to her" to help with debts from his illness, let her keep the golf shop open through Christmas until January 2, 1964, and paid his assistant, Danny Bianco, to carry on through the winter. It also gave his two sons, David and Joseph F. Jr., known as Jeffery, two years of personal golfing privileges at the club.[^ccd-minutes-1963]

## Two Josephs

This Joe is Seb's great-great-uncle. Seb's grandfather, also Joseph, was the son of Joe's brother Michael. Earlier versions of this site said the younger Joseph was named after this uncle, following the Italian custom of naming sons after relatives. That is likely, but no record states it.

media.transcription:
COUNTRY CLUB OF DETROIT. MINUTES OF MEETING OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS. HELD: OCTOBER 29, 1963.
[Page 265] GOLF, GROUNDS AND GREENS COMMITTEE

Mr. Barr announced the formation of a Committee consisting of Charles G. Chapman, Chairman, A. Fred Kammer, Jr., George Haggarty, Carlton M. Higbie, Jr., and Mrs. Harley G. Higbie, for the purpose of interviewing applicants for the position of Golf Professional left vacant by the death of Joe Belfore. The Committee will report its recommendations to the Board, however, selection of the new Golf Professional is to be made by the Board.

Mr. Higbie presented the letter of appreciation from Mrs. Belfore, and a general discussion was had regarding the handling of the Golf Shop and closing the Club accounts with the Estate of Joe Belfore. After discussion it was unanimously agreed that the Club would pay to Mrs. Belfore the sum of Seven hundred and fifty Dollars ($750.00) as a gift to her and to assist her in the settlement of obligations resulting from the long illness of her husband. On the recommendation of Mr. Higbie it was agreed that the Club would pay the sum of One thousand dollars ($1000.00) to Danny Bianco, Assistant Golf Professional, for services rendered during the past golfing season, and in addition, pay him Four hundred dollars ($400.00) for each of the months of January and February of 1964, and Two hundred dollars ($200.00) for the first half of March. Mr. Higbie stated that the Golf Shop would stay open for the Christmas Season and his recommendation that Mrs. Belfore be permitted to continue the Shop until January 2, 1964, was unanimously approved.

A discussion was had regarding the question whether and to what extent golfing privileges should be extended to David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore, sons of Joe Belfore.

On recommendation of Mr. Higbie, it was unanimously agreed that golfing privileges limited to them personally and not to guests or members of their respective families be granted to David and Jeffery Belfore, for a period of two (2) years from and after November 1, 1963. Both men shall have the right to sign chits for themselves and have the use of the Men's Grill and Locker Room.

The board voted her $750 as a gift, to help with the debts left by her husband's long illness, and agreed that she could keep the golf shop open through the Christmas season, until January 2, 1964.[^ccd-minutes-1963]

The minutes name her sons as David and Joseph F. Jr., known as Jeffery.[^ccd-minutes-1963] Earlier versions of the tree gave her first name as Ruth, but no source for it is recorded, so it is marked as unverified here.

media.transcription:
COUNTRY CLUB OF DETROIT. MINUTES OF MEETING OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS. HELD: OCTOBER 29, 1963.
[Page 265] GOLF, GROUNDS AND GREENS COMMITTEE

Mr. Barr announced the formation of a Committee consisting of Charles G. Chapman, Chairman, A. Fred Kammer, Jr., George Haggarty, Carlton M. Higbie, Jr., and Mrs. Harley G. Higbie, for the purpose of interviewing applicants for the position of Golf Professional left vacant by the death of Joe Belfore. The Committee will report its recommendations to the Board, however, selection of the new Golf Professional is to be made by the Board.

Mr. Higbie presented the letter of appreciation from Mrs. Belfore, and a general discussion was had regarding the handling of the Golf Shop and closing the Club accounts with the Estate of Joe Belfore. After discussion it was unanimously agreed that the Club would pay to Mrs. Belfore the sum of Seven hundred and fifty Dollars ($750.00) as a gift to her and to assist her in the settlement of obligations resulting from the long illness of her husband. On the recommendation of Mr. Higbie it was agreed that the Club would pay the sum of One thousand dollars ($1000.00) to Danny Bianco, Assistant Golf Professional, for services rendered during the past golfing season, and in addition, pay him Four hundred dollars ($400.00) for each of the months of January and February of 1964, and Two hundred dollars ($200.00) for the first half of March. Mr. Higbie stated that the Golf Shop would stay open for the Christmas Season and his recommendation that Mrs. Belfore be permitted to continue the Shop until January 2, 1964, was unanimously approved.

A discussion was had regarding the question whether and to what extent golfing privileges should be extended to David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore, sons of Joe Belfore.

On recommendation of Mr. Higbie, it was unanimously agreed that golfing privileges limited to them personally and not to guests or members of their respective families be granted to David and Jeffery Belfore, for a period of two (2) years from and after November 1, 1963. Both men shall have the right to sign chits for themselves and have the use of the Men's Grill and Locker Room.

people.summary: Born in New Rochelle on Christmas Day 1899, the first of the three golfing brothers. A Wykagyl shop boy who became a club professional in Duluth and Daytona Beach, taught a blind golfer to play, and later ran the 19th Hole bar on Seabreeze Boulevard.
people.story:
Sammy Belfore stood, by one sports editor's account, "just a fraction over five feet", powerfully built, with a white crest of hair and thick black eyebrows. He wore a silk ascot as a trademark. He would challenge a man to eighteen holes using only a two iron, for a side bet, and win. In his later years he was known to give a useful lesson without getting off his bar stool.[^kahn-1965][^willson-1970] He was born in New Rochelle on Christmas Day 1899, one of the nine children of Anthony and Maria Belfiore.[^standard-star-obit]

## Wykagyl

He started in golf at thirteen, in the golf shop at Wykagyl Country Club in New Rochelle, and was giving lessons by sixteen.[^kahn-1960] He told a reporter years later that he had worked in the shop for "the immortal Alex Smith", and had to wait until the members were off the course before he could sneak in a few holes before dark.[^willson-1970] Smith was a Scottish professional who won the US Open in 1906 and again in 1910, when the New York Times called him the Wykagyl professional.[^ctx-alex-smith]

That background is why the family story matters. Sammy's obituary explained that before the Belfiore brothers, golf professionals and club makers in America were almost all foreign-born, usually Scots. Sam was the first of the three American-born brothers to break through, as assistant professional at Wykagyl.[^standard-star-obit]

## White Sulphur Springs and Florida

He went on to be head professional at White Sulphur Springs, the West Virginia resort now called the Greenbrier. The Daytona papers later reported that he once beat Walter Hagen there by a stroke in a head-to-head match in 1922, and that Sam Snead succeeded him at the resort. Both stories come from Sammy's own recollections as retold in print.[^willson-1966][^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16]

He began spending winters in Daytona Beach in the 1920s. In January 1929 the News-Journal described him as "the diminutive professional at Daytona Highlands", after he shot the best individual round, a 71, at a tournament at Mount Plymouth. His brother Joe was also listed as a Daytona Highlands professional.[^dbnj-1929-01-07] Accounts disagree on when he settled for good: one column says 1924, his news obituary 1938.[^kahn-1960][^dben-1972-02-16]

## Duluth and the blind golfer

In May 1930 his engagement to Virginia Hupp was announced in Detroit by her mother, Mrs. Mae Hupp. The wedding was planned for late June at her mother's home, and the couple were to live in Duluth, Minnesota, in the summer and in Daytona Beach in the winter.[^engagement-1930]

Duluth was his summer job. He was the professional at Ridgeview Country Club there, and it was at Ridgeview that he began teaching Clinton Russell, a Duluth businessman who had been blinded in 1924 when a tire exploded in his face. Between them they worked out a method in which a caddie or friend teed the ball, set his stance for direction and lined up the clubface. In 1931 Russell shot 84 at Ridgeview, and Ripley's Believe It or Not ran the story. On August 20, 1938, Russell beat the English blind golfer W. H. J. Oxenham at Ridgeview, a match that made Time magazine.[^ouse-russell]

Earlier versions of this site put Ridgeview in Westchester and the 1938 match at Wykagyl. The Russell biography in this collection places both in Duluth.

## Daytona Beach

He was head professional at the Daytona Beach Country Club through the 1930s and into the 1940s. On March 13, 1946, he arranged a free exhibition there for Jimmy Demaret, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead and Byron Nelson. Some 4,200 people followed it, and Demaret shot 63. Fourteen years later Sammy could still recount the round shot by shot, and remembered that he had set the pins in difficult places.[^kahn-1960]

In 1947 he oversaw the restoration of the Seabreeze Golf Club for its owner, Earl Warner, and became its pro-manager when it reopened on January 1, 1948, with his brother Frank running the shop. He described the job that February in Golfdom, the golf trade magazine.[^golfdom-1948-02][^golfdom-1948-01][^kahn-1965] The local sports editor later wrote that after dark the clubhouse was a gambling house, and that some of the men who worked for it wore shoulder holsters.[^kahn-1965]

## The 19th Hole

When the club closed, he opened a bar on Seabreeze Boulevard and called it the 19th Hole. The papers give different years for the change, from 1947 to 1951.[^kahn-1960][^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16] A 1951 directory listing put it at 324 Seabreeze Boulevard, as a cocktail lounge, bar and package store.[^research-notes] He held court there for years. The jukebox played "Straight Down the Middle", and one night Rocky Marciano, retired and unbeaten, came in to see him.[^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16] Marciano's mother came from San Bartolomeo in Galdo, the town Sammy's parents had left.[^ctx-marciano] Whether either man knew that is not recorded.

He was a gambler. The same sports editor wrote that he once walked out of a dice game with $27,000 and lost it all the next afternoon on a horse-racing parlay. "I've got nobody to blame but myself," Sammy would say.[^kahn-1965] In March 1965 the sheriff padlocked the bankrupt 19th Hole, and Sammy suffered a severe heart attack the same day.[^kahn-1965][^kahn-1972]

He recovered and lived quietly at 11 South Hollywood Avenue. He died at Halifax Hospital early on Wednesday, February 16, 1972, after a stroke.[^dben-1972-02-16] A requiem Mass was said at Our Lady of Lourdes Church and he was buried at Cedar Hill Memory Gardens.[^dben-1972-02-17]

## Family

His marriage to Virginia Hupp produced a daughter, Patricia Hupp Belfore, born in 1933.[^patricia-findagrave] The marriage ended around 1939, according to earlier research.[^patricia-obit] In November 1948 the Morning Journal announced a fourth birthday party for "Little Sammy Belfore", given by his mother, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, at their home at 217 Jessamine Boulevard. A city directory entry noted in Seb's research lists Sam Belfore at that address with a wife named Louisa.[^dbmj-1948-11-20][^research-notes] His survivors in 1972 were his son Samuel M. Belfore, his daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming of Birmingham, Michigan, five sisters, and several nieces, including a Mrs. Angelia Carr.[^dben-1972-02-17]

## The name

Sammy is the brother documented as changing the spelling: his New Rochelle obituary says he "had changed the spelling of his name".[^standard-star-obit] Family tradition holds that the shorter Belfore was chosen to fit on golf scorecards. No document in this collection records the reason.[^family-knowledge]

media.alt: Newspaper clipping of Sammy Belfore's 1972 obituary from The Standard-Star, with a photograph of him swinging a club
media.summary: Summary (not a transcription). Headline: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers". Reports that Sammy, 72, died in Daytona Beach after a long illness; that he had changed the spelling of his name and had long been pro at the Seabreeze Golf and Tennis Club; that he was born on Christmas Day 1899 in New Rochelle to "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore", one of four brothers and five sisters; that Sammy, Frank and Joseph took up golf professionally when most pros were foreign-born; that Sam started as assistant pro at Wykagyl Country Club and went to Seabreeze in 1948 after 36 years in golf; that Frank ran the golf shop at the Daytona club and Joe was pro at Grosse Pointe, Michigan; that Frank, Joe and "their non-golfing brother, Michael" had died. Survivors: son Sammy Jr. (Daytona Beach), daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming (Birmingham, Mich.), sisters Rose and Caroline Belfiore (Wykagyl Gardens), Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew (Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle), Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro (Hartford, Conn.), Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio (Hollywood, Fla.), and three grandchildren. Photo caption: Sammy as he appeared in 1948 when he became golf pro at Seabreeze.

people.story:
An indexed record found in earlier research gives a Lena Belfiore, born about 1901, with parents Antonio Belfiore and Maria D. Circelli.[^lena-index] The Research page describes it as the 1940 census, but that cannot be right as written: the 1940 census does not record parents' names. The record behind the index needs to be identified.

Sammy's 1972 obituaries name nine children and no Lena.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] So either Lena died before 1972, or she is one of the five sisters under a pet name. Lena is a common Italian short form of names such as Filomena and Carolina, and both Philomena (Phyl) and Caroline were among the sisters. Her link to the family is shown with a dashed line until a record settles it.

media.caption: Country Club of Detroit minutes, page 265: the Golf, Grounds and Greens Committee report on Joe Belfore's death
media.alt: Page 265 of the Country Club of Detroit minutes of October 29, 1963, about Joe Belfore's widow, his assistant and his sons
media.transcription:
COUNTRY CLUB OF DETROIT. MINUTES OF MEETING OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS. HELD: OCTOBER 29, 1963.
[Page 265] GOLF, GROUNDS AND GREENS COMMITTEE

Mr. Barr announced the formation of a Committee consisting of Charles G. Chapman, Chairman, A. Fred Kammer, Jr., George Haggarty, Carlton M. Higbie, Jr., and Mrs. Harley G. Higbie, for the purpose of interviewing applicants for the position of Golf Professional left vacant by the death of Joe Belfore. The Committee will report its recommendations to the Board, however, selection of the new Golf Professional is to be made by the Board.

Mr. Higbie presented the letter of appreciation from Mrs. Belfore, and a general discussion was had regarding the handling of the Golf Shop and closing the Club accounts with the Estate of Joe Belfore. After discussion it was unanimously agreed that the Club would pay to Mrs. Belfore the sum of Seven hundred and fifty Dollars ($750.00) as a gift to her and to assist her in the settlement of obligations resulting from the long illness of her husband. On the recommendation of Mr. Higbie it was agreed that the Club would pay the sum of One thousand dollars ($1000.00) to Danny Bianco, Assistant Golf Professional, for services rendered during the past golfing season, and in addition, pay him Four hundred dollars ($400.00) for each of the months of January and February of 1964, and Two hundred dollars ($200.00) for the first half of March. Mr. Higbie stated that the Golf Shop would stay open for the Christmas Season and his recommendation that Mrs. Belfore be permitted to continue the Shop until January 2, 1964, was unanimously approved.

A discussion was had regarding the question whether and to what extent golfing privileges should be extended to David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore, sons of Joe Belfore.

On recommendation of Mr. Higbie, it was unanimously agreed that golfing privileges limited to them personally and not to guests or members of their respective families be granted to David and Jeffery Belfore, for a period of two (2) years from and after November 1, 1963. Both men shall have the right to sign chits for themselves and have the use of the Men's Grill and Locker Room.

people.story:
The 1963 Country Club of Detroit minutes name Joe Belfore's sons as "David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore", and grant both men two years of golfing privileges.[^ccd-minutes-1963]

Earlier research matched him to a death-index entry for a Joseph F. Belfore Jr., born August 21, 1917, who died in February 1982 in Fair Haven, Vermont.[^vt-jeffery] The match is tentative. A 1917 birth would mean his father was born by about 1897, which fits the family's other dates only if Joe was among the first children born in New Rochelle. The suggestion that his middle initial F. stands for Frank, after his uncle, is a guess with no source.

people.summary: Sammy and Virginia's daughter, born in 1933. An English and theater teacher who married John Fleming and raised four children. She died in 2022 and is buried in Birmingham, Michigan.
people.story:
Patricia Hupp Belfore was born on June 11, 1933, the daughter of Sammy Belfore and Virginia Hupp. Her middle name came from her mother's family.[^patricia-findagrave]

In 1972 both of her father's obituaries listed her as Mrs. Patricia Fleming of Birmingham, Michigan.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Earlier research, based on her own obituary, records that she taught English and theater, that she married John Fleming in 1958, that they divorced in 1990, and that they had four children: Lisa, Chris, John and Geoff. The same obituary carries a family story that she was nearly cast as Bonnie Butler in Gone with the Wind.[^patricia-obit]

She died on January 1, 2022, aged eighty-eight, and is buried at Cedar Hill Cemetery in Birmingham, Michigan.[^patricia-findagrave] Where she died is less clear: this site's golfing page says Birmingham, while earlier versions of the tree placed her in Atlantis, Florida.

Sammy's New Rochelle obituary mentions three grandchildren, while Patricia had four children. One may have been born after 1972, or the count may simply be wrong.[^standard-star-obit]

people.summary: Sammy's son, born in November 1944, probably to Sammy's second wife Louisa. He lived in Daytona and Ormond Beach and died around the end of 2024.
people.story:
On November 20, 1948, "Little Sammy Belfore" turned four. His mother, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, gave him a party at their home at 217 Jessamine Boulevard in Daytona Beach, and ten children were invited.[^dbmj-1948-11-20] That places his birth on November 20, 1944. Earlier versions of this site gave about 1935 and showed Virginia Hupp as his mother. A directory entry for the Jessamine Boulevard house names Sammy's wife as Louisa, which makes her his probable mother.[^research-notes]

When his father died in 1972, he was listed as Samuel M. Belfore of Daytona Beach.[^dben-1972-02-17] Earlier versions of the site called him Samuel Alexander, but no source for that is recorded and the 1972 records give the initial M.

He married Julia Clair. Volusia County property records show their Ormond Beach property passing to her trust in January 2025, which suggests he died in late 2024 or early 2025.[^volusia-2025]
